location_qualifier: army sector line; headquarters not stated
current_activity: Army Group G ordered to hold the line Épinal-Bains-les-Bains-Lure-L'Isle sur le Doubs-Swiss frontier from 21 September
notes: Event date: Schramm, OKW war diary, p. 394, entry of 18 September: "sei ab 21. 9. abwehrbereit" (the OCR joins "Vogesen-Stellung"); "die erreichte Linie" ... "ostwärts Lure" ... "Schweizer Grenze nördlich Damvant zu halten". Event definition: the line the Nineteenth Army held on 18 September; the order names Army Group G, and the line lies in the Nineteenth Army sector. Event support: one OKW war diary entry; the unit is the army by the sector, not by name. Location: Bains-les-Bains, a named point on the line, with a precision of 50 km for the whole sector. Location approximate: a representative point of the line. Location support fallback: the line is long; the point stands for it. Commander: General der Infanterie Friedrich Wiese.

current_activity: Wiese draws the right wing back to Montigny-Vacqueville-Bertrichamps and gives up Baccarat
notes: Event date: CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 19 p. 339: "On 31 October" "Wiese therefore obtained permission from Balck to draw the army's right wing back to the general line of Montigny, Vacqueville, and Bertrichamps, conceding the loss of Baccarat". Event definition: the withdrawal of the army right wing on 31 October; on p. 338 the LVIII Panzer Corps was ordered north on 28 October and the corps boundaries changed between 30 October and 1 November. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Vacqueville, in the middle of the new line, with a precision of 10 km. Location approximate: a line point; the army headquarters is not placed. Location support: CMH names the three villages of the line. Commander: General der Infanterie Friedrich Wiese. Opponents: French 2nd Armored Division, US 44th Infantry Division.

location_qualifier: front from the Rhine-Marne Canal to the Swiss border; the headquarters place is not named
current_activity: Nineteenth Army faces VI Corps; Army Group G moves the army boundary to the Rhine-Marne Canal
notes: Event date: CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 22 p. 405: "Army Group G pushed the boundary between the Nineteenth and First Armies to the Rhine-Marne Canal on 10 November, but the change was not fully effective until the 13th"; ch. 22 p. 389: "The LXIV Corps covered the Nineteenth Army's front from the Rhine-Marne Canal south about thirty-five miles to Saulcy-sur-Meurthe". Event definition: the boundary change of 10 November. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Colmar with a precision of 50 km, a representative point for the middle of the army front between the Rhine-Marne Canal and the Swiss border; the army headquarters place is not named in the passages read. Location approximate: a representative point for the middle of the front. Location support: CMH describes the front only. Commander: General der Infanterie Friedrich Wiese. Opponents: US Seventh Army (VI Corps) and French First Army.

current_activity: Nineteenth Army is committed to hold the Colmar bridgehead west of the Rhine after Hitler approves the new line
notes: Event date: CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 24 p. 437: "The Hitler-approved directives of 24 and 27 November committed the Nineteenth Army to the defense of a vast bridgehead west of the Rhine, a bridgehead that soon became known in the Allied camp as the Colmar Pocket"; p. 436: "OB West issued orders late on 24 November authorizing the Nineteenth Army to fall back on a new defensive line". Event definition: the directive of 27 November. Event support: one source family (CMH). Location: Colmar with a precision of 25 km, the centre of the bridgehead the army held. Location approximate: a town point for the bridgehead centre. Location support: CMH names the Colmar Pocket. Commander: General der Infanterie Friedrich Wiese. Opponents: French First Army and US VI Corps.

source_locator: R648: p. 485; R424: p. 493; R170: commander list and Gliederung, December 1944; R649: Lebenslauf and Gliederung, December 1944
current_activity: Rasp replaces Wiese as commander of the Nineteenth Army, now under Army Group Oberrhein
notes: Event date: CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 26 p. 485: "Himmler was to command Army Group Oberrhein, a new headquarters controlling Wiese's Nineteenth Army in the Colmar region"; "replaced Wiese on 15 December"; Lexikon der Wehrmacht, 19. Armee, commanders: "General der Infanterie Siegfried Rasp 15. Dezember 1944"; Heeresgruppe Oberrhein: "Dem Oberbefehlshaber Oberrhein unterstand zunächst die 19. Armee". Event definition: the change of command of 15 December in both families. Event support: two source families. Location: Colmar with a precision of 25 km, the region CMH names for the army; the headquarters place is not named. Location approximate: a town point for the region. Location support: CMH names the Colmar region. Commander: General der Infanterie Siegfried Rasp. Opponents: French First Army and US Seventh Army. Context: The sources disagree on the day Army Group Oberrhein was created (Lexikon 2 December, CMH 10 December); this claim rests on the day Rasp took over, which both families give as 15 December.
